Klasse SerialReader

java.lang.Object
treptowkolleg.plot.SerialReader
Alle implementierten Schnittstellen:
AutoCloseable
public class SerialReader extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A utility class for reading numeric data from a serial port (e.g., an Arduino) and appending it to a shared list in real time. Designed for use in live data acquisition scenarios such as voltage measurements or sensor logging.

This class automatically detects the first available serial port on startup, configures it for 9600 baud, 8N1 communication, and provides thread-safe data ingestion. It implements AutoCloseable to support safe resource cleanup and registers a JVM shutdown hook to ensure the serial port is closed gracefully on application exit.

Usage is stateful: call startReading(ArrayList) once to begin streaming data, and optionally send a trigger command via sendStartCommand(). The class is not thread-safe for concurrent initialization but is safe for concurrent reading and UI updates due to internal synchronization.

Requires the jSerialComm library (MIT licensed). If no serial port is available, the instance remains inert and all operations become no-ops.

  • Konstruktordetails

    • SerialReader

      public SerialReader()
      Constructs a new SerialReader and attempts to initialize communication with the first available serial port. If no port is found, the instance remains inactive but can be safely used (methods will behave as no-op or return false). A shutdown hook is registered to ensure clean port closure on JVM exit.

  • Methodendetails

    • startReading

      public void startReading(ArrayList<Integer> yValues)
      Starts reading serial data from the connected device and appends incoming integer values to the provided list in real time.

      This method must be called only once per instance. Attempting to start an already running reader will throw an IllegalStateException.

      Parameter:
      yValues - the list to which received integer values will be appended; must not be null
      Löst aus:
      IllegalStateException - if the reader is already running
      IllegalArgumentException - if yValues is null

    • sendStartCommand

      public void sendStartCommand()
      Sends a "start" command to the connected serial device, instructing it to begin transmitting measurement data. The command is sent as the ASCII string "start\n".

      This method has no effect if no serial port is open or if the reader is already running.

    • isAvailable

      public boolean isAvailable()
      Checks whether a serial port is available and successfully opened.
      Gibt zurück:
      true if a serial port is open and ready for communication, false otherwise

    • isRunning

      public boolean isRunning()
      Checks whether the serial reader is currently active and processing data.
      Gibt zurück:
      true if the reader is running, false otherwise

    • setRunning

      public void setRunning(boolean running)
      Sets the internal running state flag. This method is typically called by the reader itself or in response to external commands (e.g., after sending a "start" signal).
      Parameter:
      running - true to mark the reader as active, false to mark it as idle

    • close

      public void close()
      Gracefully shuts down the serial reader by stopping the reading thread and closing the serial port. This method blocks for up to 1 second while waiting for the reader thread to terminate.

      Implements AutoCloseable for use in try-with-resources statements.
